I have farmed this 0.67 hectare rice plot that my family owns since my father passed it to me. Last season I put one bag of NPK 20-10-10 and half a bag of urea on it, and the yield was good enough to pay my children's school fees and still have rice for the house. This season I will do the same because I have some cash left from selling my cassava. I also have two wheelbarrows of poultry manure from my brother's birds that I will spread before planting — it makes the soil soft and holds water. I will plant the FARO 44 seed I saved from last season; it is improved seed and it grows strong here in the South East. I do not spray chemicals because they cost too much and my family can weed by hand when the grass comes up. The rain here is plenty for rice, so I do not need to irrigate. My wife and children will work most days on the plot, and I will hire about ten days of labor from the young men in the village when we harvest because that is when we need many hands quickly.
